title: Why NASA Needed Origami to Launch a Space Telescope
description: Origami isn't just a kids' craft -- the same folding math is used to launch spacecraft and even design medical devices. AI-narrated commentary on how paper folding became real engineering.

hook_candidates.text: Everyone thinks origami is a kids' craft -- it's actually solving problems NASA couldn't crack alone.

Why did NASA need origami artists to help launch a space telescope?

beats.text: Everyone thinks origami is a kids' craft -- it's actually solving problems NASA couldn't crack alone.
In the 1980s, an astrophysicist designed a fold that lets a huge sheet collapse flat and pop open in one motion.

beats.text: NASA used that exact fold to build solar arrays that launch flat, then unfold to the size of a tennis court in orbit.

beats.text: The James Webb telescope's mirror had to fold like origami too, just to fit inside its rocket.

beats.text: Surgeons use the same math to design stents that go in tiny and unfold inside a blood vessel.
